# Provide lower-cost rendering and defer expensive work around transitions

## Platform difference

An OH port can need explicit rendering-cost and scheduling choices while keeping its Flutter UI and content model.

## Implementation

LocalSend adds a user-selectable lightweight-effects mode that removes blur/BackdropFilter, reduces shadows and substitutes gradients. Venera defers heavy reader rebuilding until route transitions complete and channel-backed work until after a frame; it uses a conservative cache fallback if the memory-info plugin is absent.

## Applicability

These are application-level strategies observed in OH-oriented forks, not evidence that Flutter effects are unavailable on the OS. The lightweight setting also affects shared visual components.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

No benchmark was reproduced. Deferral can improve transition scheduling but must not starve content or dispatch work after disposal. A conservative cache fallback is not actual memory telemetry.

## Verification

Measure frame time, memory and visual tradeoffs on representative hardware; test rapid navigation, fallback paths and user preference persistence.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
